EnableNpcGenerator.Name: Enable NPC Generator
EnableNpcGenerator.Hint: Adds a tab to NPC sheets that randomly rolls a name, instinct, and trait.

EnableMonsterGenerator.Name: Enable Monster Stat Generator
EnableMonsterGenerator.Hint: Adds a tab to NPC sheets that randomly rolls a damage die, armor, HP, and coin.

EnableAttackAssistant.Name: Enable Attack Damage Automation
EnableAttackAssistant.Hint: On a success or partial success for a melee (Hack & Slash, Backstab) or ranged (Volley, Called Shot) move, asks whether to roll damage and automatically deducts consumables like ammo. Backstab/Called Shot are recognized by the move item's own compendium ID, so they work even if not listed below.

MeleeMoveNames.Name: Melee Move Names (for custom moves)
MeleeMoveNames.Hint: Besides the moves already auto-recognized (Hack & Slash, Backstab), add the name of any homebrew melee attack move here (comma separated).

RangedMoveNames.Name: Ranged Move Names (for custom moves)
RangedMoveNames.Hint: Besides the moves already auto-recognized (Volley, Called Shot), add the name of any homebrew ranged attack move here (comma separated). Moves in this list also trigger the ammo consumption prompt.

MeleeWeaponTags.Name: Melee Weapon Tags
MeleeWeaponTags.Hint: If a weapon's tags contain any of these keywords (comma separated), it's treated as melee. Weapons have no explicit melee/ranged field; this relies on the Dungeon World convention that melee weapons use hand/close/reach. A weapon matching neither this list nor Ranged Weapon Tags still shows up in the weapon picker (it isn't excluded).

RangedWeaponTags.Name: Ranged Weapon Tags
RangedWeaponTags.Hint: If a weapon's tags contain any of these keywords (comma separated), it's treated as ranged. Dungeon World's convention is that ranged weapons use near/far. Default: near, far.

TagSettings.Title: Damage Tag Automation
TagSettings.Hint: If a checked tag is present on the weapon, its raw text is shown in the damage roll message. Tags marked "auto-applied by the damage buttons" (damage bonus / piercing / ignores armor) are picked up by Dungeon World's own full/half/double/heal damage-apply buttons when clicked — the system reads the message text itself; this module doesn't calculate anything. Those buttons apply to whichever tokens are selected on the canvas (not targeted), and require the Dungeon World system setting "Enable Damage Buttons" to be on (default: on). Tags marked "shown as a note only" (Forceful/Messy) have no system automation, so they're just displayed for the GM to judge.
